solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feeling not right in the head?

definitions.text: Feeling not right in the head?

parts.words: Feeling not right in the head?
parts.note: read as a feeling that one is unwell, which is all in the mind: imagined illness

explanation.definitionFit: Hypochondria is a persistent anxious belief that one is ill, a malady existing only in the head.

clue.text: Endlessly ran around bog producing enormous wind

indicators.note: around says the shortened word wraps the next piece
endlessly says the final letter of the word for ran is lopped off

parts.note: ran in the sense of rushed, hurried
can is slang for a toilet, as is bog

explanation.surface: Someone dashing round a marsh creates a mighty gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for a toilet, not a marsh; 'Endlessly' leaves HURRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm, a wind of enormous force.

clue.text: Country's half cut on old wine

indicators.note: half cut says the country's name is chopped in two and only its first half kept

parts.note: Portugal is the country

explanation.surface: A tipsy toper drinking vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' (British slang for drunk) halves PORTUGAL to PORT; 'on' joins it to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto is the Portuguese name for port, the fortified wine shipped from Oporto.

clue.text: Belief of socialist in company

indicators.note: in places the socialist inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A left-winger's convictions within a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Over-miserable, the French smell initially without perfume

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
dour means gloomy or miserable
les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of smell

explanation.surface: An overly gloomy Frenchman notices a smell that lacks any fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odourless gives off no scent at all, so it is without perfume.

clue.text: Plant and cultivate it on a slope, almost

parts.note: to dig the ground is to cultivate it
taken as written

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the phrase for a slope is dropped

parts.note: a list is a lean or slope, so a slope is a list

explanation.surface: A gardener told to grow a plant on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims A LIST (list being a tilt, as of a ship) to ALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is the foxglove genus, a flowering plant also yielding a heart drug.

clue.text: Passage opening covered by paint roller

indicators.note: covered by says the letters sit concealed within the words paint roller

explanation.surface: A passage whose entrance is coated with a decorator's roller.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music or writing, an introduction.

clue.text: By chance bra let loose giving complete freedom

indicators.note: loose says the letters of chance bra let are freed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Letting a bra slip at random gives total liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche, French for blank paper, means full licence to act as one wishes.

clue.text: One's used to dry song by Queen

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tune performed by Her Majesty that is rather dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame on which washing is hung to dry.

clue.text: Fluid end with legato stretched out

indicators.note: fluid says the letters of end and legato flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical ending played smoothly and drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongated means lengthened, drawn or stretched out.

clue.text: Agreed it isn't working, so break up

indicators.note: working says the letters of the phrase are worked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Two parties agree a scheme has failed, so they part.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into fragments.

clue.text: Common European standard

parts.note: read as a widespread EU norm, but a standard is a flag, and many European flags have three bands

explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a three-coloured flag, a type of standard seen across Europe in France, Italy and others.

clue.text: Tory leader goes off for jogs

indicators.note: leader takes the opening letter of Tory

parts.note: to go off is to rot, as food does

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief heads out for some runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Trots means jogs, running at an easy pace.

clue.text: Bar in club containing case of Edelzwicker

indicators.note: containing says the club holds the next letters within it

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the 2-wood

indicators.note: case of takes the outer letters of Edelzwicker

explanation.surface: A drinking spot in a nightclub stocking a case of Alsace wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Edelzwicker is an Alsatian blended white wine; only its outer letters E and R are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal bar-restaurant, originally French and serving beer.

clue.text: Confused clash involving mob I fancy

indicators.note: fancy used as an adjective, elaborate or fanciful, signals reworking the letters

explanation.surface: A muddled skirmish with a crowd that I imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal British for chaotic or disorganised, hence confused.

clue.text: Judge in person detaining former wife? It's automatic

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is a judge of play

indicators.note: detaining says the phrase for in person holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a live appearance is one in person
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Does a referee in person holding back an ex-wife act on instinct?
explanation.definitionFit: A reflexive action is an involuntary reflex, done without thought.

clue.text: It's yellow getting Trotsky around Mexican capital

indicators.note: around says the first name wraps the next letter

parts.note: Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

indicators.note: capital takes the opening letter of Mexican

explanation.surface: Something yellow linked to Trotsky, killed near Mexico City.
explanation.walkthrough: Trotsky was assassinated in Mexico, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is the name of a pale yellow colour as well as the yellow fruit.

clue.text: Line from man he ties at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of man he ties are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rope coming from a sailor who knots it on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainsheet is the rope controlling a sailboat's mainsail; on board ropes are lines.

clue.text: One playing 'Leader of the Pack'?

parts.note: read as a performer of the pop song, but here one who takes the role of a pack's leader

explanation.definitionFit: Akela, the wolf in The Jungle Book, names the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack.

clue.text: Implement for sashimi?

parts.note: sashimi is sliced raw fish, so a kitchen tool is jokingly read as producing it

explanation.definitionFit: A fish slice is a broad slotted kitchen utensil for turning or serving fish.

clue.text: Titbit about peculiar Bishop

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning an eccentric cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny piece, a morsel or titbit.

clue.text: Brown is more insensitive losing head

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter

parts.note: number is the comparative of numb, more lacking feeling

explanation.surface: Someone tanned grows less sensitive after a beheading.
explanation.walkthrough: Read NUMBER as 'more numb', not the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy brown pigment, and the colour named after it.

clue.text: He should get the devil out!

definitions.text: He should get the devil out!

parts.words: He should get the devil out!
parts.note: read as an exasperated remark about a troublesome man, but literally describes one who expels demons

explanation.definitionFit: An exorciser drives evil spirits out of a person or place.

clue.text: Check inside mineral for pigment

indicators.note: inside places the check abbreviation within the mineral

parts.note: ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Examining a rock for traces of colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy clay pigment, yellow to red-brown.

clue.text: Stunner that is trim on top

indicators.note: on top places the trim word above the other in this down entry

parts.note: to trim is to cut
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A beauty who looks neat on top, with a fresh haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive person, a looker or stunner.

clue.text: Deck in mayhem? Bell is hammered

indicators.note: hammered says the letters are beaten into a new order
in says a short word lies within mayhem

explanation.surface: A church in chaos as its bell is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks HEM out of 'mayhem'; 'hammered' scrambles HEM with BELLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or decorate, which is to embellish.

clue.text: River burst beyond head of tide

indicators.note: beyond places the burst word after the letter from tide
head of takes the opening letter of tide

parts.note: rent, past of rend, means torn or burst

explanation.surface: A river bursts its banks past the tidal head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a long river in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Iron, say, liquid metal centre containing energy

indicators.note: containing says the rearranged letters hold the next one
liquid says the letters of metal centre flow into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Molten metal at the core holding energy, such as iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges METAL CENTRE to TRACELEMENT, and 'containing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is an example of a trace element, needed by the body only in tiny amounts.
